extracted.intended_audience: statistical practitioners, leaders/supervisors/mentors, and organizations conducting official statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts ethical and procedural standards for statistical practice aimed at individual practitioners, supervisors/mentors, and organizations, including responsibilities, misconduct handling, and alignment with OMB/NASEM/OMB data-ethics standards and statistical policy directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides feedback or advice that is impartial, constructive, and objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides feedback or advice that is impartial, constructive, and objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as an expectation in the context of interacting with the work of others through appropriate peer review or consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Takes full responsibility for contributions as instructors, mentors, and supervisors
rubrics_metrics.description: Takes full responsibility for their contributions as instructors, mentors, and supervisors of statistical practice by ensuring their best teaching and advising -- regardless of an academic or non-academic setting -- to ensure that developing practitioners are guided effectively as they learn and grow in their careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes duty of care in training and supervision; applies across academic and non-academic settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotes reproducibility and replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotes reproducibility and replication, whether results are 'significant' or not, by sharing data, methods, and documentation to the extent possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages sharing of data, methods, and documentation to support reproducibility even for non-significant results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serves as an ambassador for statistical practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Serves as an ambassador for statistical practice by promoting thoughtful choices about data acquisition, analytic procedures, and data structures among non-practitioners and students. Instills appreciation for the concepts and methods of statistical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy and education role directed at non-practitioners and learners; fosters appreciation of statistical concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle G: Ensure appropriate statistical practice (leaders/supervisors/mentors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure appropriate statistical practice that is consistent with these Guidelines. Protect the statistical practitioners who comply with these Guidelines, and advocate for a culture that supports ethical statistical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies specifically to those leading, supervising, or mentoring; includes advocacy and protection of compliant practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle G: Promote respectful, safe, productive work environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote a respectful, safe, and productive work environment. Encourage constructive engagement to improve statistical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders should foster constructive engagement and psychological safety to improve practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle G: Identify/create professional development opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and/or create opportunities for team members/mentees to develop professionally and maintain their proficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible for enabling ongoing professional development and proficiency maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle G: Advocate inclusion and appropriate recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocate for appropriate, timely, inclusion and participation of statistical practitioners as contributors/collaborators. Promote appropriate recognition of the contributions of statistical practitioners, including authorship if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders should ensure practitioners are included and properly credited; authorship requires explicit permission because it may imply endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle G: Establish culture valuing validation and assessment of models/algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a culture that values validation of assumptions, and assessment of model/algorithm performance over time and across relevant subgroups, as needed. Communicate with relevant stakeholders regarding model or algorithm maintenance, failure, or actual or proposed modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes ongoing validation, subgroup assessment, and communication about maintenance and failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle H: Know misconduct definitions and procedures; clarify facts and intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Knows the definitions of, and procedures relating to, misconduct in their institutional setting. Seeks to clarify facts and intent before alleging misconduct by others. Recognizes that differences of opinion and honest error do not constitute unethical behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be informed about institutional policies; avoid premature allegations; distinguish honest error/from misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle H: Avoid condoning or appearing to condone misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoids condoning or appearing to condone statistical, scientific, or professional misconduct. Encourages other practitioners to avoid misconduct or the appearance of misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active discouragement of misconduct and its appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle H: Do not make poorly founded or intimidating allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Does not make allegations that are poorly founded, or intended to intimidate. Recognizes such allegations as potential ethics violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False or intimidatory allegations themselves can constitute ethics violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle H: Lodge complaints discreetly to relevant institutional body
rubrics_metrics.description: Lodges complaints of misconduct discreetly and to the relevant institutional body. Does not act on allegations of misconduct without appropriate institutional referral, including those allegations originating from social media accounts or email listservs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow institutional channels; avoid public or informal adjudication via social media/email lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle H: Insist upon transparent and fair adjudication; maintain confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Insists upon a transparent and fair process to adjudicate claims of misconduct. Maintains confidentiality when participating in an investigation. Discloses the investigation results honestly to appropriate parties and stakeholders once they are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance transparency in adjudication with confidentiality during investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle H: Refuse to publicly discredit reputation while due process continues
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuses to publicly question or discredit the reputation of a person based on a specific accusation of misconduct while due process continues to unfold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect reputations until investigation concludes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle H: Support resumption of careers consistent with investigation outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Following an investigation of misconduct, supports the efforts of all parties involved to resume their careers in as normal a manner as possible, consistent with the outcome of the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aid in rehabilitation or career resumption where appropriate given findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle H: Avoid and discourage retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoids, and acts to discourage, retaliation against or damage to the employability of those who responsibly call attention to possible misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect whistleblowers and those who responsibly raise concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Expect and encourage adherence to Guidelines (organizational responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expecting and encouraging all employees and vendors who conduct statistical practice to adhere to these Guidelines. Promoting a workplace where the ethical practitioner may apply the Guidelines without being intimidated or coerced. Protecting statistical practitioners who comply with these Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations must foster environments where adherence is possible and protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Engage competent personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging competent personnel to conduct statistical practice, and promote a productive work environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations should hire/retain personnel with appropriate competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Promote professional development and proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting the professional development and maintenance of proficiency for employed statistical practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations should support training and continuing education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Support objective and transparent statistical practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting statistical practice that is objective and transparent. Not allowing organizational objectives or expectations to encourage unethical statistical practice by its employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent organizational pressures from leading to unethical choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Recognize authorship/acknowledgement requires explicit permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing that the inclusion of statistical practitioners as authors, or acknowledgement of their contributions to projects or publications, requires their explicit permission because it may imply endorsement of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain explicit permission before listing practitioners as authors or acknowledging contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Avoid exploitative or discriminatory statistical practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoiding statistical practices that exploit vulnerable populations or create or perpetuate discrimination or unjust outcomes. Considering both scientific validity and impact on societal and human well-being that results from the organization’s statistical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations must weigh ethical and societal impacts alongside scientific validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Use professional qualifications as basis for personnel decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Using professional qualifications and contributions as the basis for decisions regarding statistical practitioners' hiring, firing, promotion, work assignments, publications and presentations, candidacy for offices and awards, funding or approval of research, and other professional matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions about practitioners should be merit-based on qualifications and contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Recognize reporting only expected results is contrary to Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing that it is contrary to these Guidelines to report or follow only those results that conform to expectations without explicitly acknowledging competing findings and the basis for choices regarding which results to report, use, and/or cite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full reporting of competing findings and rationale for selection is required to avoid bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Recognize results cannot be guaranteed to conform to sponsor expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing that the results of valid statistical studies cannot be guaranteed to conform to the expectations or desires of those commissioning the study or employing/supervising the statistical practitioner(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations and leaders should accept uncertainty and integrity of valid results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Objectively, accurately, and efficiently communicate statistical work
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectively, accurately, and efficiently communicating a team’s or practitioners’ statistical work throughout the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure internal communication is accurate and objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Represent ethical issues fairly to leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where ethical issues are raised, representing them fairly within the organization's leadership team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring ethical concerns to leadership attention objectively and fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Manage resources and strategy consistent with ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Managing resources and organizational strategy to direct teams of statistical practitioners along the most productive lines in light of the ethical standards contained in these Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate resources and set strategy that enable ethical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey Planning Standard 1.1: Develop a written plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey Planning Standard 1.1: Develop a written plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should document planning for concepts, methods, and design in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey Design Standard 1.2: Develop a survey design
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey Design Standard 1.2: Develop a survey design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choices should be documented and appropriate for survey objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey Response Rates Standard 1.3: Design to achieve highest practical response rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey Response Rates Standard 1.3: Design the survey to achieve the highest practical rates of response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design should aim to maximize response while balancing other constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretesting Survey Systems Standard 1.4: Ensure all components function
rubrics_metrics.description: Pretesting Survey Systems Standard 1.4: Agencies must ensure that all components of a survey function as intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pretest systems end-to-end to verify intended operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 2.1: Ensure sampling frames are appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing Sampling Frames Standard 2.1: Ensure that the frames for the planned sample survey or census are appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames should be suitable representations of the target population for intended inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 2.2: Required notifications to potential survey respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Required Notifications to Potential Survey Respondents Standard 2.2: Agencies must ensure that each collection of information instrument clearly states the reasons the information is planned to be collected; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruments must clearly state purposes and provide required notifications to respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 2.3: Data collection methodology (balance quality against error; minimize burden/cost)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Collection Methodology Standard 2.3 (BALANCE QUALITY AGAINST ERROR, MINIMIZE BURDEN/COST).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design data collection to balance data quality and error reduction while minimizing respondent burden and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Editing Standard 3.1: Agencies must edit data appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Editing Standard 3.1: Agencies must edit data appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement appropriate editing procedures consistent with preserving data quality and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 3.2: Nonresponse analysis and response rate calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonresponse Analysis and Response Rate Calculation Standard 3.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze nonresponse and calculate response rates to assess potential bias and data quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 3.3: Coding quality for others to use
rubrics_metrics.description: Coding QUALITY FOR OTHERS TO USE Standard 3.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code data in a way that is useful and interpretable for other users, with clear documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Protection Standard 3.4: Avoid disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Protection Standard 3.4 AVOID DISCLOSURE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement disclosure avoidance and data protection consistent with confidentiality obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Standard 3.5: Agencies must evaluate the quality of the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation Standard 3.5: Agencies must evaluate the quality of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly evaluate data quality using appropriate measures and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 4.1: Developing estimates and projections using theory and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing Estimates and Projections USING THEORY AND METHODS Standard 4.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate theory and statistical methods when developing estimates and projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 5.1: Analysis and report planning; develop a plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis and Report Planning Standard 5.1: Agencies must develop a plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare analysis and reporting plans prior to analysis to guide transparent and reproducible work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 5.2: Inference and comparisons - use acceptable statistical practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Inference and Comparisons Standard 5.2: USE ACCEPTABLE STATISTICAL PRACTICE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply accepted statistical inference methods and justify methods used for comparisons and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 6.1: Review of information products - review what is disseminated & comply with OMB GLS
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of Information Products Standard 6.1: REVIEW WHAT IS DISSEMINATED & COMPLY WITH OMB GLS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review dissemination products to ensure compliance with OMB Government-wide Statistical policies and guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 7.1: Releasing information - use an equitable plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Releasing Information Standard 7.1 (USE A PLAN THAT IS EQUITABLE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt equitable dissemination planning for release of information products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 7.2: Data protection and disclosure avoidance for dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Protection and Disclosure Avoidance for Dissemination Standard 7.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply disclosure avoidance techniques and data protection measures in dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 7.3: Survey documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey Documentation Standard 7.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide adequate survey documentation to support transparency and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 7.4: Documentation and release of public-use microdata
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation and Release of Public-Use Microdata Standard 7.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and release public-use microdata with appropriate protections and metadata for users.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.1: Methodological plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard A.1: Methodological Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a documented methodological plan as part of SPD2a requirements (methodological planning).

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.2: Sample selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard A.2: Sample Selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and justify sample selection procedures; ensure appropriateness for study goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.3: Interview guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard A.3: Interview Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare interview guides consistent with SPD2a methodological planning and instrument design.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.4: Systematic analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard A.4: Systematic Data Analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct systematic analysis following documented procedures and methods; ALIGN with Appendix guidance where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.5: Transparent analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparent Analysis Standard A.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure analyses are transparent, including methods, assumptions, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.6: Final reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Reports Standard A.6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce final reports that document methods, findings, and limitations appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPD2a Standard A.7: Reporting results
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting Results Standard A.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report results fully and accurately with attention to context, uncertainty, and potential impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRI1: Relevance to policy issues and society
rubrics_metrics.description: PRI1 Relevance to Policy Issues and Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical activities should be relevant to policy and societal needs; alignment tables show mapping to ASA principles and OMB directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRI2: Credibility among data users and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: PRI2 Credibility Among Data Users and Stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain methods and communications that support credibility with users and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRI3: Trust among the public and data providers
rubrics_metrics.description: PRI3 Trust Among the Public and Data Providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect confidentiality and act to maintain public trust and willingness to provide data.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRI4: Independence from undue external influence
rubrics_metrics.description: PRI4 Independence from Political and Other Undue External Influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguard independence of statistical activities from improper pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRI5: Continual improvement and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: PRI5 Continual Improvement and Innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster continual improvement in methods and innovation consistent with quality and ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRA1: Clearly defined and well-accepted mission
rubrics_metrics.description: PRA1: A Clearly Defined and Well Accepted Mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical organizations should have a clear mission that guides practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRA2: Necessary authority and procedures to protect independence
rubrics_metrics.description: PRA2: Necessary Authority and Procedures to Protect Independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations should have authority and procedures that protect independence of statistical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRA3: Commitment to quality and professional standards of practice
rubrics_metrics.description: PRA3: Commitment to Quality and Professional Standards of Practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to professional standards and quality assurance practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRA4: Professional advancement of staff
rubrics_metrics.description: PRA4: Professional Advancement of Staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support staff development and career advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRA5: An active research program
rubrics_metrics.description: PRA5: An Active Research Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an active research program to improve methods and capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRA6: Strong internal and external evaluation processes
rubrics_metrics.description: PRA6: Strong Internal and External Evaluation Processes for an Agency’s Statistical Programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement rigorous evaluation processes to assure quality and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRA7: Coordination and collaboration with other statistical agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: PRA7: Coordination and Collaboration with Other Statistical Agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with other agencies where appropriate, while taking precautions to avoid conflicts with independence or ethical guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRA8: Respect for data providers and protection of their data
rubrics_metrics.description: PRA8: Respect for Data Providers and Protection of Their Data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect respondent rights and data confidentiality; consider impacts on individuals and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRA9: Dissemination of statistical products that meet users’ needs
rubrics_metrics.description: PRA9: Dissemination of Statistical Products That Meet Users’ Needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design dissemination to serve user needs while protecting confidentiality and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASEM PRA10: Openness about sources and limitations of the data
rubrics_metrics.description: PRA10: Openness About Sources and Limitations of the Data Provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about data sources, methods, limitations, and uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T1: Uphold statutes, regulations, and ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: T1. Uphold applicable statutes, regulations, professional practices, and ethical standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with legal/regulatory requirements and recognized professional/ethical standards in statistical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T2: Respect the public, individuals, and communities
rubrics_metrics.description: T2. Respect the public, individuals, and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider societal consequences and respect rights and dignity of affected populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T3: Respect privacy and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: T3. Respect privacy and confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect personal and sensitive information and limit uses consistent with consent and law.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T4: Act with honesty, integrity, and humility
rubrics_metrics.description: T4. Act with honesty, integrity, and humility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate limitations and uncertainty; avoid overstating conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T5: Hold oneself and others accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: T5. Hold oneself and others accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accountability mechanisms for practices and decisions, including addressing misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T6: Promote transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: T6. Promote transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open about methods, decisions, and limitations to build trust and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Data Ethics Tenet T7: Stay informed of developments in data management and data science
rubrics_metrics.description: T7. Stay informed of developments in the fields of data management and data science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuously update skills and practices in light of methodological and technological advances.
